subject: Staged fallback checks, network fabric validation, and ops sim
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>; Ava Ramos <ava.ramos@acme-payments.com>, netops-team@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Staged fallback checks, network fabric validation, and ops sim

Team —

Ahead of the scheduled traffic shift for Acme on Monday, I want to kick off a quick run of the staged-fallback checklist and a low-risk ops sim to validate the network fabric and our rollforward/fallback paths. Goals:

- Confirm fabric adjacency rules and BGP peering after the planned config push.
- Verify traffic mirroring + canary receives identical routing and no path asymmetry.
- Execute a runbook playback of a fallback to cold pool and confirm KV cache warmup behavior.

I've attached the checklist and a template for recording canary metrics. Proposed schedule:
- Friday 11/28 15:00 PST — dry-run (no traffic) runbook playback w/ ops bridge
- Monday 11/30 02:00 PST — staged traffic shift to 10% for 30 minutes (customer-aware window)

Marissa / Markus — can you confirm availability for the Friday bridge and who from infra should be on-call?

Connor
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops_staged_fallback_checklist_v1.pdf, runbook-playback-notes.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ava Ramos <ava.ramos@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged fallback checks, network fabric validation, and ops sim

Connor —

I can be on the Friday bridge at 15:00 PST. I'll bring the runbook owner (SRE lead) and the on-call network engineer. Preliminary confirmations:
- SRE: Markus Klein (will run the playback)
- Network: Soojin Lee (will validate adjacency and BGP state)

Action items before Friday:
1) Markus to prep an isolated canary namespace and share endpoints.
2) Soojin to script a BGP state snapshot and a quick comparison tool.
3) Ops to seed KV cache priming keys into the canary path.

I'll attach the canary namespace manifest after Markus spins it up.

Marissa
Director, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ava.ramos@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-28T11:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged fallback checks, network fabric validation, and ops sim

All good — I'll own the playback and capture timestamps for each run step. Notes for the checklist:
- Playback will include: traffic-shift simulation, deliberate route flap to trigger fallback, KV cache drain/warmup measurement, and validation of observability spans.
- I plan to use a synthetic load generator pointed at the canary namespace; results saved to canary-observed-metrics-1129.csv (attached after validation).
- If we see >2s tail latency on the canary path for more than two consecutive samples, we'll abort and roll back.

One ask for Soojin: can you confirm the emergency fallback path has traffic-engineering (TE) weight set correctly (10 -> 0) during a rollback? I want to be sure the fallback doesn't create transient blackholes.

Markus
SRE Lead, Private Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-28T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged fallback checks, network fabric validation, and ops sim

Quick update from netops prep:
- BGP sessions validated on the east and west peering routers; no flaps in the last 72 hours.
- I uploaded a BGP snapshot script to the Drive link so the bridge can invoke it at step 2.
- TE weights checked; emergency fallback path will accept traffic when primary weight drops below threshold — this is configured and tested in lab.

Two caveats:
1) The cloud vendor's public egress ASN is being patched on their side Sunday; if that slips into Monday we should push the traffic-shift back. Ava, can you flag if your provider schedules anything?
2) KV cache priming: the canary path will see an initial latency hit until priming completes — we've accounted for it in the rollback criteria.

Soojin
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

Also: can you share the exact rollback play (step-by-step) so our network team can mirror the checks? They want to validate that health checks will failover cleanly.

Ava Ramos

Subject: Friday dry-run notes and Friday bridge readout

Thanks everyone for joining the dry-run. Short readout attached — highlights below and next steps.

Highlights (from runbook-playback-notes.txt):
- BGP snapshot tool executed at step 02: no adjacencies lost.
- Simulated route flap successfully redirected traffic to emergency fallback; TE weights behaved as expected.
- KV cache priming completed in ~45s; initial 95th p95 increase to 180ms during priming window.
- Canary metrics saved to canary-observed-metrics-1129.csv (attached).

Decisions:
- Proceed with Monday 10% staged shift, hold if Acme's provider hasn't confirmed the Sunday maintenance is transparent.
- Ops bridge on Monday: Connor (bridge lead), Marissa (runbook owner), Markus (SRE playback), Soojin (networker), Acme NetOps on standby.

Next actions:
1) Ava to confirm provider maintenance by 2026-11-29 22:00 PST.
2) Markus to seed canary metrics and share final csv.
3) Marissa to publish the rollback step-by-step to the shared Drive link.

Connor
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary-observed-metrics-1129.csv, runbook-playback-notes.txt
